principles: Root stays reserved for stable entrypoints, user-owned notes, and standard repository files.
Agent-generated durable documentation belongs under canonical docs truth-source locations.
Documentation cleanup must not fabricate capability, Production Safety, authority, or unattended-readiness claims.
drivers: The user explicitly wants root clutter removed and jek.md preserved as user-owned.
The previous guide still allowed the legacy Koala root guide to remain, which conflicts with the clarified policy.
Root document moves need a precise plan before implementation to avoid broken links and truth-source drift.

options.name: A: Write execution solution and align existing guide now
pros: Creates a concrete implementation path without risking immediate broken links.
Corrects the old guide so the legacy Koala root guide is no longer retained.
Keeps this story scoped to docs and lets migration happen in a later implementation story.
cons: Does not remove the root files yet.
Requires a follow-up execution story to perform moves/deletes.

options.name: B: Move/delete root docs immediately in this story
cons: Could mix planning, content merge, compatibility stubs, and deletion into one high-risk change.
Could accidentally imply Production Safety or capability state changes.

options.name: C: Only answer in chat, no repository doc
cons: No durable project truth source for future agents.
The existing guide would still say the legacy Koala root guide may remain.

chosen: A: Write execution solution and align existing guide now
rationale: Choose A because the user asked for an execution document and a solution, while the repository needs a durable plan before risky root-file moves. This also fixes the existing guide policy conflict without pretending that the cleanup has already been executed.

preMortem.scenario: The solution still leaves the legacy Koala root guide as an allowed root file.
preMortem.trigger: The new doc copies the prior compatibility language instead of applying the clarified user policy.
preMortem.consequence: Future agents preserve root clutter and the user sees no practical path to cleanup.
preMortem.mitigation: State that the legacy Koala root guide is a retirement target and should not remain as an allowed root file after migration.

preMortem.scenario: The execution plan overclaims migration completion.
preMortem.trigger: The doc says root files are moved or cleaned before any actual move/delete story runs.
preMortem.consequence: Repository state and documentation diverge, causing false DONE-like confidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Use future-tense execution gates and explicitly say this story writes the solution only.

preMortem.scenario: High-risk capability or Production Safety files are merged into existing unlock docs without review.
preMortem.trigger: The plan treats all Lattice root docs as simple low-risk moves.
preMortem.consequence: The docs imply capability or Production Safety readiness that has not been reviewed or validated.
preMortem.mitigation: Route high-risk files to boundary/history handling with no-unlock/no-claim language and a separate implementation review.
